department: Department of Environmental Sciences (Graduate School of Arts and Sciences)

deadline.value: Apply by January 15 for full financial-aid consideration; later applications are reviewed but aid may not be available.
deadline.quote: Applications received by January 15 will receive full consideration for financial aid

gre_general.value: GRE scores are neither required nor accepted.
gre_general.quote: GRE scores: We do not require, nor do we accept, submission of GRE scores.

gre_subject.value: GRE scores of any kind are neither required nor accepted.
gre_subject.quote: GRE scores: We do not require, nor do we accept, submission of GRE scores.

supervisor.value: Admission is largely driven by a match with a faculty adviser; contact recruiting faculty before applying (listed on the page for Fall 2027).
supervisor.quote: we recommend applying to the M.S. and Ph.D. programs only if you find a potential fit with a faculty adviser

funding.value: PhD admission comes with a stipend, tuition and health insurance (GTA/GRA); duration is set in the offer letter, and the Graduate School guarantees five years.
funding.quote: Admission to our M.S. and Ph.D. programs comes with financial aid including stipend, tuition, and health insurance.

also.quote: The Graduate School offers doctoral students a minimum of five years of financial support upon admission

entry_route.value: No specific undergraduate degree is required; admitted students typically have a science or engineering bachelor's.
entry_route.quote: We do not require any specific undergraduate degree, and admitted students typically have a range of undergraduate majors across science and engineering.

notes: One PhD covers ecology, geosciences, hydrology and atmospheric science, so earth is listed in also_fields.
